text:
Trevor Zegras's second season in Philadelphia has been quiet in the wrong way. He has one goal and three points in his last ten games, and the Flyers have been buried when he's on the ice at five on five: 38% of the expected goals, more than eight points worse than the team without him.

That last number is the one to sit with, because it's not who he was a year ago. Evolving-Hockey had him as one of the better play-drivers in the league in 2025-26, worth 2.1 wins with his team creating more with him on (94th percentile among forwards) against tough competition. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had his offense living on the rush, 55% of his shots in transition.

Some of this is bad luck. He has five goals on 7.2 expected, and the Flyers have scored 7.3 fewer goals than their chances with him out there, so our range has his scoring rate a little above where it sits. The effort criticism is landing too: Charlie O'Connor pinned a Buffalo goal on him getting knocked off the puck too easily by Peyton Krebs.
